questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When riding over an uneven surface, rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently than usual to protect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe only when using the front brake.
Safe only when using the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is not as easy as braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must use proper technique and be very careful.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good method.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire to test it.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire that is under-inflated may still look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also provides extra protection if you crash.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which of these is not a hazard:

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Wind blasts.
Headlights.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Also be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects that might be thrown by its passengers.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment begins:

options.text: Well below the legal limit.
At the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment starts well below the legal limit.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Passing another vehicle.
You will slow down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals do not work.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as visible as a car's two larger brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps others see it, especially when you need to slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: As your weight shifts forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight moves forward while braking, the front wheel gets more traction. This means you can apply the front brake with more force.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead at the road for:

options.text: Road conditions.
Traffic conditions.
Escape routes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Look ahead to stay alert to traffic changes, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: Long rides in cold weather can cause all of the following, except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: During a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle together. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When riding in a group, less experienced riders should ride:

options.text: At the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way they won't fall behind. More experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, the rider should:

options.text: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean away from the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while their body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black text show traffic rules like speed limits. Follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more dangerous than on a car. Always check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: To be seen in a car's rearview mirror ahead of you, ride:

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left side of the lane.
In the right side of the lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: If you follow a car, position yourself in the center of your lane. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between the cars to pass quickly.
Not weave between the cars.

questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors may open or cars may pull into traffic suddenly. You won't have room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night instead of during the day, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam when possible.
Follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, what should a motorcycle operator be ready for?

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A driver suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers seeing your motorcycle and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to suddenly enter traffic. It is safest to ride on the left side of your lane when parked cars are on your right. This gives you the most space between your motorcycle and any danger.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it, no matter what.
Change lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting a car.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a requirement for an effective eye or face shield?

options.text: Free of scratches.
Resistant to breaking.
Fastens securely.
Completely sealed from air.

questions.explanation: Good eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist breaking, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. They should also give a clear side view and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you on your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Swerve around the dog.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, shift down and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride alongside the dog.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, shift down and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions to help them stay safe.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, how often should you use both brakes?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.
Not very often.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, where should you position your motorcycle in your lane?

options.text: Toward the right side of your lane.
Toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane.
